Finding1: q6/b256 has essentially no large dispatch gap. Kernel CP =69.778/71.607/76.359ms vs root-ready-to-last-kernel =70.341/72.025/76.789ms. Difference only0.563/0.418/0.429ms and root startup accounts0.325/0.314/0.345ms of it. CPU CP differs by merely0.013–0.014ms from wall CP. A prior49ms serial-cost estimate cannot be compared as a schedule-independent lower bound: kernels take longer in the actual parallel/cache/CPU context. Changing wake/queue alone has no20ms opportunity on this observed q6 run.

Finding2: q12/b128 has potential order-of-a-few-ms scheduling opportunity. Envelope27.75–28.66ms, measured weighted CP22.68–26.04ms, gating-ready waits3.46–5.46ms including0.33–0.36ms startup. Gating waits with24 kernels active =2.90/4.97/3.29ms; rep2 another1.25ms had23 active. Most important waits therefore happen while cores are doing other work, not asleep with no tasks. Requires better choice of ready work, not simply more wakeups; do not rerun previously failed generic priority experiments without a new reason.

Finding3: real kernel CPU cost, not Linux preemption, dominates q6. Summed wall minus CPU across56 calls =0.065–0.068ms total; madd mean CPU9.25/9.57/9.73ms (min7.28–7.49, max12.78–15.87). First update layer mean CPU10.08/10.82/10.40ms; final single update7.93/8.31/7.93ms. q12 later update layers likewise about0.92–0.96ms vs early/central layers about1.2–1.5ms. Correlates with concurrent conditions and working sets, but no PMU means cache contention, frequency and core class cannot be separated.

Finding4: there is real block migration, useful evidence for the locality agent. Of35 repeated-output transitions in q6,22–27 cross worker IDs; of286 in q12,187–211 cross IDs. This is evidence to test generic output ownership, not proof it wins: active operands, dependencies and worker load differ. Slow worker IDs are not stable across runs; do not bake CPU IDs or local topology guesses into production.

Finding5: idle machinery consumes CPU despite small critical latency. q6 summed worker nonkernel CPU57.3/59.8/61.8ms,4540/4637/4894 CV wait entries across24 workers. q12 nonkernel CPU19.2/24.1/21.2ms,786/816/810 waits. This CPU sum is not elapsed overhead; reducing it can help only if it improves actual kernel execution/resource contention or startup. Prior idle tuning negatives remain binding; this observation alone is not a new candidate.

READ-ONLY PROPOSAL — current base3429b75, no build/test/numeric workload/production edits.

Observed code: runtime.cpp289 ready transitions use push(publisher,target), and atomic work396-401 retains the newest ready target as a private continuation. Thus the last predecessor worker determines placement, even if a different worker previously updated that target's output region. Ready queues already use localLIFO and thiefFIFO. This favors producer/input reuse but gives no stable output home. No evidence of migration frequency or actual cache misses yet: that is a hypothesis, not a measured bottleneck.

Proposed distinct candidate: SOFT OUTPUT-REGION OWNERSHIP, an optional RuntimeOptions output_locality=false (root approval needed; parent main/benchmark exposes selector). Per graph, compute preferred_owner[task] from the largest nonempty write region (ties follow source region order); hash only logical buffer identity and offset/rows/cols/stride with cheap integer mixing. Equal exact regions map to the same allowed worker; distinct regions spread without the power-of-two alignment skew of offset%workers. Collisions harmless because hints only affect placement. Read-only/no-write tasks retain publisher-local behavior (sentinel worker count). No Cholesky symbols, q formulas, n/b assumptions, source/case names or metadata fields.

Implementation scope runtime.cpp plus one optional flag parent can append to core. SetupO(total declared writes + buffer-name bytes),uint32 preferred owner[n] =~78KB at19600 tasks. Cache vector allocation/reservation included in pre-execution estimate and reserved_bytes; clear at drained boundary. Root can later consolidate with compact-task arena if validated; no Task/header representation rewrite needed now.

Ready transition routing:
- atomic final decrement still acq_rel exactly once. If target's preferred owner equals current worker (or no hint), it may take existing private continuation; otherwise enqueue immediately to hinted ready queue.
- owner backend dependency inbox ownership stays target%workers (unchanged), but once remaining reacheszero enqueue to preferred ready queue. Do not conflate counter ownership with placement.
- initial zero-indegree tasks go to preferred owner or existing i%workers fallback.
- work stealing scans all ready queues as today, so affinity is soft; idle cores do not wait for a homeworker. No sticky/nonstealable tasks, no artificial dependencies or global barriers.
- notify_one is sufficient for generic ready work even if homeworker is parked because any wokenworker can steal; owner inbox notify_all staysunchanged.

Correctness: graph edges/counts, operator calls,args and numerical order on conflicting writes unchanged. Queue mutex release/acquire plus existing final acq_rel gather preserve predecessor visibility on crossworker publish. Only one final-decrement winner publishes each target; private continuation only selected for local owner, never simultaneously queued. Empty/read-only/multiplewrite/mixedbuffer/overlappingregion tasks remain correct—geometry hash is placement hint only, not dependence decision. Hash collisions change speed only. Failure drain and run reuse unchanged; storage setup before numeric hook. Explicit owner backend still serviced despite remote readyplacement.

Expected upside: repeated updates of one output tile may stay in a core cache, avoiding dirty-line migration acrossprivate caches. This targets real kernel memory locality, unlike already-rejected priority rank or completion counter batching. Read inputs also travel; output reuse may sacrifice producer locality and increase remote queue traffic. Existing thieves may immediately defeat homeownership when few ready tasks; narrowheavy q6 may notbenefit. Arbitraryhash can spread load but uneven dependency frontiers may queue behind busyworker. No promised speedup or bound without parent kernel/CPUwait profile. One-time O(V) owner setup adds cost to tiny cases; default-off untilrootA/B.

Suggested minimum validation after compile slot: independent DAG correctness/visibility/exactonce withsameoutput repeated writes,fanout/diamond,readonly,emptyregions,multiwrite,multibuffer,deliberateowner collisions;1/4threads,atomic/owner,batch1/3;exceptions+reuse;budgetfailurebefore numeric hook. Existingpublic20+R27 functional gate. Metadata141B unchanged. No permanenttests or per-taskdiagnostic output in production.

Requested root decision: approve flag/API + runtime-only prototype, or await kernel/cache profile first. Parent owns formal scoring and main/benchmark switch; no compile allowed untilassigned. If actual A/B noise/noimprovement, reject completely rather than layeringsticky policies.
